prompt: Your team runs a Raft-backed coordination service that provides distributed locks and leader election for the rest of the platform. Right now every read — including dashboard and metrics queries — goes through the code below, which unconditionally calls `readIndex()`, a majority-heartbeat round-trip that confirms current leadership before ever touching the local store. Under load this round-trip dominates read latency, even though only lock-acquisition and leadership-decision reads actually require linearizability; a stats endpoint being a few tens of milliseconds stale is harmless. How would you restructure this read path so the expensive confirmation is paid only where staleness would be a correctness bug, while display-only reads are served nearly free from the local replica?
